generators.carrier: Rat (nc, nf) -> Rat; finite rational model of the 1-loop coefficient
Python Fraction-valued beta_0(N_c, n_f) = (11/3) N_c - (2/3) n_f

relations.statement: (4 : Rat) * suNCasimirAdjoint 3 + (-1/3 : Rat) * suNCasimirAdjoint 3 = 11 and qcdBeta0 3 0 = 11, together with the recorded window values of qcdBeta0 3 nf
relations.hypotheses: finite rational model; N_c = 3; no continuum or running-coupling content

relations.statement: qcd_beta0(n_c, n_f) = 11*n_c/3 - 2*n_f/3 as an exact rational; at n_c = 3 this is 11 - (2/3) n_f
Test checker confirming the Gross-Wilczek-Politzer beta0 values agree with the rational formula in the finite model

lemmas.statement: qcdBeta0 3 nf takes the values 11, 9, 23/3, 7, 1/3, -1/3 at nf = 0, 3, 5, 6, 16, 17 (exact rational arithmetic inside the finite model only)
lemmas.lean_skeleton: theorem qcd_beta0_window_values : FiniteQM.qcdBeta0 3 0 = 11 ∧ FiniteQM.qcdBeta0 3 3 = 9 ∧ FiniteQM.qcdBeta0 3 5 = 23/3 ∧ FiniteQM.qcdBeta0 3 6 = 7 ∧ FiniteQM.qcdBeta0 3 16 = 1/3 ∧ FiniteQM.qcdBeta0 3 17 = -1/3 := by sorry

near_misses.claim: The positive window 0 <= n_f <= 16 establishes asymptotic freedom of the continuum running coupling, a mass gap, a weak-coupling limit, Monte Carlo spectroscopy, or higher-loop MSbar matching
near_misses.rejecting_invariant: The research map withholds these: the certificate is finite rational arithmetic only and says nothing about a running coupling in a continuum theory
Exact recomputation: 11 - 32/3 = 1/3; the value -1/3 occurs at n_f = 17
